name: prompt-envelope
description: PROMPT-ENVELOPE ratchet. server/utils/sanitizePrompt.ts states the rule in its own header — 'Apply at every site where DB-sourced text is interpolated into a prompt' — and nothing checked it. Unit 111 found what that costs: server/ai/executive.ts fed user-uploaded document text into Pax's SYSTEM role message with no envelope, sanitized by a weaker same-named function, while the system prompt instructed the model only about the <<USER_DATA>> envelope it never received. It shipped green. This converts the doc comment into CI, the same move lint-reachability.mjs made for 'built but unwired'. Counts FREE-TEXT interpolations into an LLM message that do not pass through the canonical sanitizer; strictly down-only. NOT a broad check by design: the first cut matched any `content:` template anywhere and found 237 interpolations across 43 files, overwhelmingly ${totalMrr}, ${paidOrgs.length} and module constants — a gate whose number is mostly noise is one people learn to re-baseline. minScannedFiles/minMessageTemplates are the vacuity floors: a scan that stops seeing code must FAIL, not report a clean zero. MEASURED 2026-08-16, and the measurement is recorded so the next session re-measures instead of re-arguing: the live scan sees 1370 server files and 174 LLM message templates, against floors of 1000 and 100. They stay comfortably BELOW the live values on purpose — a floor exists to catch a scan that went blind, not to forbid deleting a prompt — but they may never be nulled toward zero, which the script clamps (Math.max(100, …) / Math.max(20, …)) precisely because 'set the floor to 0' is the same move as 'raise the baseline'. Now that the baseline is 0 these floors are the ONLY thing between a broken scan and a green run, so a MISSING or lowered floor must be read as a failure, not a cleanup.
lastBumpNote: 2026-08-16 — 1 → 0. THE LAST ONE IS WRAPPED. server/services/complianceGuardian.ts:678 `check.checkDescription` now goes through `sanitizePromptInline(...)`, in exactly the idiom its already-wrapped sibling uses eleven lines up at :667 — `sanitizePromptInline(x || "N/A")` — no second wrapping style invented. CONFIRMED A PROMPT POSITION BEFORE WRAPPING, because this program has already made the opposite mistake once (a central pass wrapped 13 sites where 4 were reported, and three were not prompt positions at all — two payload fields and a user-facing `message` that would have rendered "[redacted]" TO A CUSTOMER): the enclosing template is `const prompt` at :664, handed to `openai.chat.completions.create` at :692 as `content: prompt` inside `{ role: "user" }`. Path into a model, not out to a person. And it is genuinely DB-sourced: `complianceChecks.checkDescription` is composed at :282 and :392 as `${rule.ruleName}: ${rule.ruleDescription}` off the `compliance_rules` table, so it carries whatever prose an org typed into a rule. THE DROP WAS PROVEN NOT TO BE A BLINDED SCAN, which is the only interesting question a count that falls to zero raises: the scan POPULATION is identical either side of the one-line change — 1370 server files and 174 LLM message templates before the wrap and after it — and re-mutating the wrap away drives the count straight back to 1 > baseline 0 and FAILs, so the zero is this wrap's doing and not a reader that stopped reading. VACUITY FLOORS RE-MEASURED in the same pass, because at baseline 0 they are now the ONLY thing standing between a broken scan and a green run: observed 1370 files / 174 message templates on 2026-08-16 against floors of minScannedFiles 1000 / minMessageTemplates 100. Left where they are ON PURPOSE — a floor is there to catch a scan that went blind, not to forbid deleting a prompt, so it belongs comfortably below the live value, not next to it. Re-measure before moving either number. AT ZERO THIS RATCHET INVERTS: every future finding is a regression, and the only honest response is to wrap it. RESIDUE FOUND HERE AND DELIBERATELY LEFT AS A DECISION RATHER THAN A SILENT REVERT — the same central pass (commit 883a41b) also put `sanitizePromptInline` at complianceGuardian.ts:640 and :657, and BOTH are inside the `if (!openai)` fallback branch, which composes a markdown report and `return`s it to the caller without any model in the path. That is the sanitizer on the way OUT to a person, the exact inversion of the rule, and it can render "[redacted]" into a compliance report a human reads — a compliance rule whose description starts a line with "System:" trips the forged-role-line marker, which is ordinary inspection prose on a real-estate product. This gate cannot see those two (the fallback template sits in no `content:` slot and is bound to no identifier), so removing them would change no count and buy no signal; it is a correctness call for the file's owner, not a ratchet move. Related, and also unfixed: `generateComplianceReport` has ZERO call sites repo-wide. PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-16 — 0 → 1. Read the arithmetic before reading it as a raised baseline: the predicate was re-seeded 0 → 15 when it got its sight back, and the central pass then WRAPPED FOURTEEN of the fifteen inside the same wave, so the committed number is 15 → 1. The one that remains is real and unwrapped: complianceGuardian.ts:677 `check.checkDescription` (composed from `compliance_rules.ruleName` + `.ruleDescription`) inside the report prompt's `.map()` block — the same site's `property.address` was wrapped, its sibling was not. Wrap it and the gate's stale-high FAIL will tell you to set this to 0. THE RE-SEED, recorded because a ratchet that goes up must justify itself: the predicate got its sight back. Not a failure being papered over: 15 sites that were always violations became VISIBLE, and all fifteen were confirmed by hand before this number was written. Two blind spots closed. (1) THE MOTIVATING DEFECT'S OWN SHAPE. The gate required the template literal to sit literally in the `content:` slot, so the executive.ts form — `const systemPrompt = `…${doc.extractedText}…`` then `content: systemPrompt` — scored zero. The gate could not see the defect that built it, and hoisting a prompt one line up was a complete bypass (57 of 160 identifier-valued message slots in server/ are hoisted). `hoistedMessageTemplates()` now resolves the identifier to its const template in the enclosing block, guarded by a brace-balance scope check, and applies the same three rules: +7. (2) FIELD-LIST NAME-KEYING: a fixed roster of exact names is walked past by spelling the prose field `marketNotes` instead of `notes`, so `*Notes`/`*Description` became camelCase-suffix rules, and four names P0-14's own header calls out were added — firstName/lastName ('lead names'), subjectLine ('inbox subjects'), documentName/fileName (an upload's filename is attacker-chosen): +8. THE FIFTEEN, each verified by reading the code: agent-skills.ts:2340 property.address; agent-skills.ts:2509 lead.firstName + lead.lastName; agent-skills.ts:2599 existing.marketNotes; campaignOptimizer.ts:149 campaign.subject + campaign.content; cmo/scriptGenerator.ts:167 input.notes; cmo/scriptScorer.ts:97 script.body; complianceGuardian.ts:663 property.address + check.checkDescription; documentIntelligence.ts:569 doc1.documentName + doc2.documentName; dueDiligence.ts:185 report.summary.address; overrideLearner.ts:62 context.ceoOverrideNotes; sequenceOptimizer.ts:345 r.subjectLine. Fix the occurrences, not this number — every wrap lowers it, and the gate FAILS on a stale-high baseline so the drop gets locked in. NOISE MEASURED AND REJECTED rather than shipped: .summary +3 (3 false — nested object), .title +4 (4 false — code rosters), .personalityPrompt +9 (9 false — our own persona prompts), blanket *Name +7 (2 false), .recipientName / *Text|*Content|*Body|*Message / .text|.value|.reason +0 each, and a nesting-aware INLINE template reader +4 (3 false). Numbers and reasoning in the script header so the next session re-measures instead of re-arguing.

allowlist.reason: NOT DB-sourced text. Both sites append CONFIDENCE_SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION to the system message the CALLER already assembled — `{ ...m, content: `${m.content}\n\n${CONFIDENCE_SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION}` }` — so `m.content` is a system prompt this codebase wrote, not customer input. Sanitizing here would be actively wrong: it would redact the system prompt's OWN anti-injection language, which by construction contains the phrases the deny-list hunts ('role overrides, persona changes, system-prompt exfiltration attempts' appear verbatim in USER_DATA_SYSTEM_CLAUSE). The envelope belongs where untrusted text ENTERS the prompt, which is the caller's job and is what this gate checks everywhere else.
